_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED, MERGED. Ghana was researched as a parallel split this session, per Thomas's instruction at the end of AF/G.3.md: Claude took the core LEAP-formula/GSS-CPI mechanism lane; Grok took the funding/donor architecture, other Ghanaian benefit programmes, and Ghana's international-statistics standing. Both halves are combined here, per Thomas's standing instruction ([[feedback_grok-as-verification]]) that Grok's quoted, sourced, confidence-tagged answers are minted directly -- with one exception, see _open_questions. Several of Claude's own findings (the CPI rebase to 2021=100, the SSNIT indexation quote, the World Bank GPSNP2 quote, Act 1148's assent date) were pulled independently via direct WebFetch, some overlapping with and cross-confirming Grok's round rather than only extending it. Sitting in src/data/research/ alongside the other Africa drafts pending review.
_note: Ghana turns out to have the same evidentiary shape as Ethiopia's UPSNJP finding, not Kenya's: a real, specific, quoted formula (LB_t+1 = LB_t(1+inf_t), capped at 50%, GSS-CPI-based -- MOFEP's own Sep 2023 strategy paper) that multiple independent sources (Ghana's Graphic Online, via a MoGCSP/MoF joint announcement) describe as having actually taken effect from late 2023/2024, well before any statute caught up to it. The Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148) -- independently confirmed by both this session's own fetch and Grok's round to have been assented and commenced 14 August 2025 -- establishes the Social Protection Fund and covers LEAP by name in secondary reporting, but its full operative text sits behind a judy.legal paywall; only the Application and Object sections (generic, no indexation language) were freely readable. So the graph can show the formula (real, quoted, already implemented per press reporting) and the Act (real, dated, scoped to LEAP per secondary sources) but NOT a document-to-document link between them -- MOFEP's 2023 paper cites only 'the proposed Social Protection Bill', a forward reference to an unnamed future bill, not Act 1148 by number. Treated the same way the corpus already treats Ethiopia's constitution/World-Bank pair: an observed consistency (same programme, same ministries, plausible timeline), not an edge, because no document names the other by its actual title. If the Act's full text or its Legislative Instrument (expected June 2026) becomes readable, check specifically for an operative indexation clause -- see _open_questions.

_open_questions.question: Whether the Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148) itself contains an operative CPI-indexation clause for LEAP, or only establishes the Social Protection Fund/framework while indexation remains cabinet-level policy pending the Legislative Instrument (submitted to Parliament, expected in force by June 2026 per MoGCSP). Full text is paywalled at judy.legal (https://www.judy.legal/legislation/akn/gh/act/2025/1148); no free official gazette or parliament.gh copy was located by either this session or Grok's round.

Grok's round reported that in June 2025 the ECOWAS Council of Ministers adopted a Regulation relating to a Methodological Guide for compiling a regional Harmonised CPI (COICOP 2018, 13 functions) -- the potential West African analogue to Kenya's binding EAC HCPI regulation. This session ran two independent, differently-worded searches for the regulation's title, number, or any ECOWAS-hosted document and found zero corroboration -- not even a passing news mention. Not minted as a node for lack of any document. Worth a direct reprompt to Grok asking specifically for the regulation's exact title/number and a working URL before this is trusted, per the standing policy's own carve-out for oddly-specific, unsourced claims.

reports.title: Strategy Paper on Index-Linking LEAP Benefits to Inflation
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance (Ghana), with the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (direct fetch of the strategy paper itself). States the indexation formula precisely: 'LB_t+1 = LB_t(1 + inf_t)' where inf_t is 'the 12-month annual average inflation from October of previous year to September of current year estimated from Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) Consumer Price Index release', with annual adjustments 'capped at 50%'. States the mechanism 'will be backed by legislation to enhance its effectiveness and continuity... through the proposed Social Protection Bill' -- a forward reference to an unnamed future bill, not a citation of Act 1148 by number (Act 1148 did not yet exist). On funding: 'The primary source of funding the LEAP Programme should be GoG resources. However, opportunities for alternative funding support, particularly from development partners, should be identified and explored.' Cites the World Bank's Social Protection Public Expenditure Review as a data source for its own figures. Independently corroborated as actually implemented (not merely proposed) by Ghana's Graphic Online, reporting the mechanism 'will take effect from this month to enable an automatic adjustment of grants', introduced through 'collaborative work between the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP), and the Ministry of Finance (MoF), after increasing the allowances paid to beneficiaries by 100 per cent in 2023', with a further GH₵720 million committed in the 2024 budget for an additional 12% increase.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (Ghana Statistical Service)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via GSS's own CPI Technical Methodology Manual (v5, published October 2020) and its own recent press releases. The v5 manual: 'GSS uses 13 out of the 15 Divisions as distinguished by the COICOP manual', organised into '44 Groups, 98 Classes, 156 Subclasses, and 307 Item-level observations', and 'to order products into these different categories, GSS uses the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 manual.' Elementary aggregates: 'GSS uses the unweighted Jevons Index... the geometric mean of price relatives.' The v5 manual describes the then-current series on 'the whole year of 2018 as the price reference period' with 'weights based on the Ghana Living Standard Surveys 7 (GLSS7) from 2016/2017', and credits input from 'Statistics Denmark, and the International Monetary Fund (IMF)' plus ILO CPI-manual guidance. GSS has since rebased: the September 2025 press release (published 1 October 2025) states 'the price reference period has been updated to 2021 (2021=100)' with the weight reference period still 2017 -- confirmed independently, distinct from and more current than the v5 manual's own 2018=100 description. The rebase's own dedicated methodology note (as opposed to a press-release mention) was not located this session.

release_schedule.note: GSS publishes CPI/inflation monthly, consistently in 'Week 1' (occasionally week 2) of the month following the reference month. Observed 2026 releases: May 2026 CPI released ~June 4, 2026; June 2026 CPI released July 1, 2026; July 2026 CPI released Aug 6-7, 2026 (inflation 4.6%). GSS's own 2025 Statistical Product Release Calendar PDF confirms CPI is scheduled in Week 1 (or Week 2) of each month, but states the calendar 'will be updated quarterly' and no 2026 edition with exact dates was found online, so the September 2026 (for August 2026 data) date is inferred from the pattern rather than a published calendar entry.

reports.title: Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP)
reports.description: Ghana's flagship cash-transfer programme. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via MoGCSP's own LEAP background page: established under Ghana's Growth and Poverty Reduction Strategy II (GPRS II), 'first disbursement in March 2008 to 1,654 pilot households across 21 districts.' Now indexed to inflation via the mechanism described in gh-mofep-leap-indexation-strategy, per Graphic Online's reporting that the indexation mechanism 'took effect' following the 2023 strategy paper. Development-partner support (World Bank, UNICEF, UK Government/FCDO) is acknowledged on the programme's own page without a stated funding split; see gh-gpsnp2-worldbank for the current primary World Bank financing instrument and its own stated split (GoG now the larger share).

reports.title: Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148)
reports.description: Ghana's framework social-protection statute. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session against judy.legal's hosted text (an Akoma Ntoso-identified official-text mirror, the same convention used by Kenya Law for ke-social-protection-act-2025) and independently corroborated by Grok's round: passed by Parliament 31 July 2025, 'assented to on 14 August 2025' and 'commenced on 14 August 2025' as Act 1148. Section 1 (Application) covers 'chronically poor', 'economically at-risk', 'socially vulnerable', and persons 'affected by a national or a local emergency'. Section 2 (Object): to 'reduce poverty and vulnerability', 'promote the well-being' of those groups, and foster 'sustainable livelihoods and decent work'. Secondary reporting (MoGCSP, news coverage) states the Act establishes a Social Protection Fund and explicitly covers LEAP and the Ghana School Feeding Programme by name, but the free public preview only exposes Sections 1-2 -- no operative indexation clause was independently readable. The implementing Legislative Instrument (LI) was, per MoGCSP, submitted to Parliament and expected in force by June 2026. See gh-mofep-leap-indexation-strategy for the earlier (2023) formula this Act may or may not put on statutory footing, and _note for why no edge connects the two documents.

reports.title: Ghana Productive Safety Net Project 2 (GPSNP2)
reports.description: The World Bank/IDA project currently financing LEAP, effective January 2022. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session, quoting the project's own text: development objective 'to expand and enhance social safety nets that improve the incomes and productivity of the poor in Ghana.' Component 3 'supports the continuation, expansion, and strengthening of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) program through increased coverage, improved targeting, higher benefit levels, and enhanced capacity of decentralized implementation structures', delivering 'bimonthly cash transfers to poor households using digital payment systems and targeting based on the Ghana National Household Registry data.' Financing: IDA credit US$100.0 million, Government of Ghana counterpart US$157.0 million; Component 3 (LEAP) specifically allocated US$177 million total (US$20 million IDA, US$157 million GoG) -- i.e. Ghana's own government is now the majority funder of the LEAP component, distinct from the earlier Ghana Social Opportunities Project and first GPSNP (2010s), which per Grok's round carried GBP 21 million in FCDO co-financing. This is the direct evidentiary counterpart to Ethiopia's SEASN/PSNP5 project financing (et-psnp5-worldbank-seasn), confirming a comparable donor-financing-instrument-names-the-programme-it-funds shape for a second country in this branch.

reports.title: SSNIT Pension Indexation Rate (annual review and announcement)
reports.publisher: Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT)
reports.description: SSNIT's annual review of pensions in payment, published as a dedicated press release each year. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via SSNIT's own 2025 Pension Indexation Rate press release, which cites its legal basis as 'Section 80 of the National Pensions Act, 2008 (Act 766)' and quotes the statutory standard: 'The Trust shall annually review the pension payment which shall be indexed to wage inflation rates of active contributors or another rate determined by the Trust in consultation with the Board of the Authority.' The same press release lists the factors SSNIT considered for the 2025 rate: 'Average salary of active contributors from the previous year', 'Annual average Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the previous year', 'Affordability and the impact of indexation on the cost of pensions to the Scheme', and 'The effect of indexation on the long-term sustainability of the Scheme' -- CPI is a named, explicit input but one of four, not a standalone formula; the statute's own default reference is wage inflation, with CPI and other factors used in the Trust's alternative-rate determination. Act 766's own text was not independently fetchable this session (the government registry copy blocks automated access); this description rests on SSNIT's own quotation of its governing section. Grok's round adds an unverified-by-this-session 2026 example: an overall 10% indexation (fixed 6% plus a redistributed flat GH₵91.56), against SSNIT's own stated ~5.4% end-2025 inflation figure -- i.e. the review outcome is deliberately not a pure pass-through of CPI, consistent with the four-factor statutory language.

entries.covers: 2025 pension indexation rate announcement (announced Jan 6, 2025 at 12%)
2026 pension indexation rate announcement (announced Jan 8, 2026 at 10%)

release_schedule.note: SSNIT has no published release calendar or statutory fixed date for the indexation announcement, but it has consistently announced the new year's pension indexation rate (approved by its Board) in the first half of January each year: 2023 (Jan 13), 2024 (January), 2025 (Jan 6), 2026 (Jan 8). This is an observed annual pattern, not a stated rule, hence next occurrence is projected as January 2027.

dependencies.basis: The strategy paper's own formula computes directly from GSS's release: 'inf_t = 12-month annual average inflation from October of previous year to September of current year estimated from Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) Consumer Price Index release' -- a named, direct computational input, not background context.

GPSNP2's own Component 3 text names and funds LEAP directly: 'supports the continuation, expansion, and strengthening of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) program' -- a donor financing instrument describing the programme it funds, the same relationship shape as et-psnp5-worldbank-seasn -> et-psnp5-design-document.

SSNIT's own 2025 indexation press release lists 'Annual average Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the previous year' as one of four named factors in the statutory Section 80 review -- a direct, named input into the Trust's determination, even though the review is not a single CPI-only formula.

GSS's own CPI Technical Methodology Manual: 'To order products into these different categories, GSS uses the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 manual.' Reuses the un-coicop-2018 node first minted for South Africa/Nigeria (za-fiscal-federalism.json) -- a fourth country now confirmed on the current COICOP vintage, alongside South Africa, Nigeria and Kenya, versus Egypt's older COICOP-HBS 1999/2000.

Ghana's own Ministry of Finance press release (November 2018) announcing IMF Statistics Department support: 'The Mission supported the development of the National Summary Data Page (NSDP), which will be accessible from the Coordinating Agency website', describing implementation of 'the IMF's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System', which 'supersedes the GDDS, which was established in 1997.' Reuses the imf-e-gdds node first minted for Kenya (ke-social-protection.json) and also carried by Ethiopia (et-psnp-cpi-federalism.json) -- Ghana is now a third country confirmed on the weaker (non-SDDS) IMF dissemination tier, independently dated to November 2018 on the national side, matching Grok's round's citation of the same month from a 2026 IMF Article IV report.

_dropped.why: Ghana's National Daily Minimum Wage is set annually by the National Tripartite Committee under Section 113 of the Labour Act, 2003 (Act 651), per Grok's round. Grok reports the Committee 'considers inflation (GSS CPI), cost of living, productivity, business sustainability, and employment levels' -- but this is a negotiated outcome among multiple factors, not a formula, and organised labour has itself publicly criticised the process for leaning too heavily on the inflation figure rather than applying it automatically (also per Grok's round). No node was minted for the minimum-wage mechanism at all: this session did not independently verify Act 651 s.113's text, and even a confirmed quote would describe a discretionary negotiation rather than a documented computational dependency of the kind this graph records.

Grok's round reported a June 2025 ECOWAS Council of Ministers Regulation adopting a Methodological Guide for a regional Harmonised CPI (COICOP 2018, 13 functions) as the West African analogue to Kenya's binding EAC HCPI regulation. Two independent, differently-worded searches this session for the regulation's title, number, or any ECOWAS-hosted document found nothing -- no corroborating source, no URL, not even a passing news mention. Not minted as a node; see _open_questions for the recommended follow-up.
